Incorporating the Beige Book, the FOMC’s March 2018 statement is reinforced by on‑the‑ground reports of broad employment gains and strong demand for qualified workers, alongside rising wage pressures. District anecdotes indicate employers are raising wages and compensation, with some firms citing the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act as a contributor to compensation decisions. These details strengthen the case for the Committee’s view that labor market conditions will remain strong and that inflation should drift toward 2 percent, even as the policy stance remains accommodative after the 25 bp hike to 1.50–1.75 percent.

Credit conditions from the January SLOOS remain supportive near term—easing in C&I for large and middle‑market firms—while offsets persist: tighter standards and softer demand in CRE (especially construction and land development) and mixed consumer credit with anticipated performance deterioration in credit cards and HELOCs. Together with elevated valuations and corporate leverage risks, these argue for the FOMC’s gradual path.

Netting the Beige Book’s stronger labor and wage signals with the mixed credit picture leaves the near‑term outlook modestly more positive than January but still consistent with a prudent, gradual normalization path.
